description.narrative: Forty years of armed conflict, recurrent natural disasters, chronic poverty, drought and the COVID-19 pandemic have devastated the people of Afghanistan. The full impact of the recent take-over of power by the Taliban is not yet clear but the recent political developments have pushed Afghanistan into another humanitarian and economic crisis.

The AFJR is targeting some of the most vulnerable people, women (including PLW), children (with a special focus on CU5), elderly/ chronically ill and disabled people in particular. Although assessments showed that they are affected differently, they are bearing the brunt of the crisis.

Through the AFJR intervention, SCI support the humanitarian response system through integrated health, nutrition, WASH and multi-purpose cash response which will lead to reduced mortality and morbidity, improved health and nutrition outcomes, ensuring communities affected by multi-faceted humanitarian crises are protected from all forms of violence, abuse, and neglect through integrated assistance.
